source: Poulopoulou, Modern Greek: Grammar Notes for Absolute Beginners (A1-A2), ΣΕΑΒ/Kallipos 2015, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 GR (upload 8e8e722c), Chapter 6 (book pp. 82-91; 6.6 possessives not in the uploaded pages)
note: Complements declensions.json personal_pronouns by adding strong vs weak accusative usage and the other pronoun classes.

rules.rule: Weak form is the object, placed right before the verb, after δεν.
rules.el: Σε αγαπάω πολύ. / Δεν σε θέλω.
rules.en: I love you very much. / I don't want you.

rules.rule: Strong form after a preposition; initial ε- often drops after a stressed vowel.
rules.el: Αυτό το δώρο είναι για (ε)σένα. / από σένα

rules.rule: Weak 3rd-person accusatives equal the definite article accusative and replace only definite nouns.
rules.el: Θέλεις τον καφέ σου; Ναι, τον θέλω. / Θέλεις καφέ; Ναι, θέλω.
rules.en: Do you want your coffee? Yes, I want it. / Do you want coffee? Yes.

with_αρέσει.rule: The liked thing is the nominative subject with the definite article; the verb agrees with it.

demonstrative.rule: Used alone like 3rd-person pronouns, or before a noun with an obligatory definite article.

examples.el: Αυτός θέλει παγωτό, εκείνος θέλει μπίρα.
examples.en: This one wants ice cream, that one wants beer.

ποιος.note: One syllable, so no accent mark. Masculine is the default (Ποιος είναι;).

τι.meaning: what; what sort of (before a noun)

examples.en: How much sugar do you want?
How many bananas do you want?

interrogative.rule: A preposition comes before the question word: Για ποιον είναι το δώρο;

indefinite.rule: κάποιος/κάτι in affirmative sentences; κανένας/τίποτα in questions and negatives. Greek has no 'no one': use δεν + κανένας. Elliptical Τίποτα still means 'anything'.

forms.κανένας: καν- + indefinite article (κανέναν, καμία/καμιά, κανένα); no plural

που.note: Unaccented; interrogative πού is accented. όπου can replace που meaning 'where'.

examples.en: Here is the map I want.

examples.el: Θέλω τον χάρτη που είναι στο τραπέζι.
examples.en: I want the map which is on the table.

examples.el: Να το σπίτι που / όπου μένω.
examples.en: Here is the house where I live.
